A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HeteroCache. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, with retained content identifiable across reflow and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, latency measurements, component ablations, threshold sensitivity tests, and attention-head analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds calibration-transfer, multi-needle retrieval, resource-consumption, and latency experiments.

M1.justification: The head taxonomy, allocation equations, and retrieval algorithm remain unchanged. However, Appendix C.2 deletes v1's statement about adding a numerical smoothing term to inverse-stability weights. Because the equations and pseudocode omit this term in both versions, the PDFs do not resolve whether the procedure changed or only its description.

E1.justification: v2 adds 128K natural-document calibration using LongBench Pro tasks involving code/version differences, numeric reasoning, and dialogue tracking. It also adds multi-needle U-NIAH evaluation beyond the retained single-needle NIAH experiment. These extend represented data and retrieval requirements while preserving the original benchmarks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the original experiments is unchanged: FullAttention, Quest, ShadowKV, OmniKV, and CAKE retain their respective participation. The new U-NIAH comparison uses FullAttention, and the consumer-hardware experiment uses FullAttention and CAKE; neither introduces a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Added protocols include 20 calibration samples per task at 128K with top-k set to one-fifth of context length, ROUGE-1 evaluation on U-NIAH, 1K-token generation for latency analysis, and RTX 4090/PCIe Gen3 testing. The original 50-token mean-latency protocol remains. The reported main CPU changes from Xeon 6326 at 2.90 GHz to 6338 at 2.00 GHz, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 adds calibration sensitivity and transfer analyses using satellite-head overlap and downstream Qasper performance. Appendices D.2 and D.4 investigate CPU memory, bandwidth consumption, retrieval frequency, latency tails, and constrained interconnects. These substantially extend v1's component ablations, threshold sensitivity, and cross-model taxonomy analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new P95/P99 measurements characterize per-token latency performance, rather than uncertainty across repeated experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their values. New results include Qasper scores of 45.61–45.72 under alternative calibration, over 80% satellite-head overlap, 17.95 GB peak CPU memory and 21.07 GB/s bandwidth at 128K, U-NIAH scores, and additional latency measurements. Appendix D.4 reports a 0.823% retrieval-trigger rate. These are newly reported outcomes under added conditions, not improvements to retained benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 retain the same overlap, stability, similarity, allocation, and drift definitions. Algorithm 1's indexing and GPU/CPU notation edits are mathematically equivalent. No new theorem, proof, or formal derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: training-free heterogeneous KV compression using head profiling, stability-based allocation, and asynchronous retrieval. The state-of-the-art performance and up-to-3× decoding acceleration claims remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning calibration transfer, resource scalability, multi-needle dependency retention, and generation stability. Its limitations discussion narrows the bandwidth caveat to extremely low-bandwidth environments after the consumer-hardware test. These extend applicability arguments while retaining the original mechanism explanations.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised future code release with a repository link and adds detailed RAM, GPU capacity, memory-bandwidth, and PCIe specifications in Table 6. It also documents the consumer-hardware setup and calibration cost. The main CPU specification is revised, and Appendix C.2 removes the previous smoothing-term disclosure.

R1.justification: LongBench Pro and U-NIAH are newly cited, and the overlap-coefficient attribution changes from McGill to Szymkiewicz. The overall related-work positioning remains stable. Updated DeepSeek-R1 and star-clustering references correspond to already cited work rather than new research directions.

P1.justification: v2 polishes the abstract and several paragraphs, changes 'decaying' heads to 'shifting' heads, updates affiliations, and adds acknowledgments and cross-references. Appendix C.4 and a new Appendix D extend the existing organization; the LLM-use statement moves to Appendix E. Most prose and the main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 5–10 add substantial displays covering calibration, hardware, resource consumption, multi-needle retrieval, and latency. Figure 1 receives revised typography and labels, and captions and page placement are adjusted. The original benchmark tables and result figures, including Appendix Figure 6, are retained.

improvement.justification: The added calibration-transfer, resource-consumption, and long-generation latency analyses address practical questions that v1 largely left untested. Code-access information and hardware details also improve reproducibility. The gain is limited by broad interpretations of the selected calibration studies and consumer-hardware timings that mostly show near parity. The revision strengthens practical validation without fully establishing its stronger applicability conclusions.
